Van Wortswinkel, L., & Nijs, W. (2010). Iron and Steel. IEA ETSAP Technology Brief I02. https://iea-etsap.org/E-TechDS/PDF/I02-Iron&Steel-GS-AD-gct.pdf

Two denominations in one document. Table 1's first block (blast furnace and COREX) is EUR2010; Table 1's second block (Midrex, Hylsa, Tecnored, Hismelt, EAF) and every cost in the body text are USD2000, which p.4 states explicitly. Neither a deflator nor an exchange rate is given. Nothing converted.

Table 1's two blocks do not share a column layout - five columns in the environmental block against six in the cost block, which splits Tecnored into cogeneration and non-cogeneration. All columns were resolved from the PDF's x-coordinates; read in text order the headers interleave and produce wrong column names, and the sparse rows (coke, burnt lime, iron ore fines, sinked CO2) land under the wrong technologies.

Changes against the repo copy: (1) two temperature-output rows moved to _process-temperatures.csv - the plasma blast furnace's 2150 degC is a calculated flame temperature and the coke oven's 1000-1100 degC is the coal charge temperature, neither a delivered-heat temperature; the coke oven's hand-computed midpoint 1050 and its formula were dropped. (2) The coke oven's two derived flow rows used a 0.775 midpoint (1.29 t coal and 419 Nm3 COG per t coke); they are now ranges derived from the printed 750-800 kg coke and 325 m3 COG per 1000 kg coal with both ends converted (1.25-1.333 t coal and 406.25-433.33 m3 COG per t coke), unit m3 as printed. The flue-gas temperature (1150-1350 degC) is added to _process-temperatures.csv. (3) blast-furnace_coal notes now start with their context in brackets: '[p.1 and p.4 body text, US$2000]' for the 148-275 USD capex, '[Table 1, EUR2010 block]' for the Table 1 rows - two contexts of one example, not reconcilable (no exchange rate). No process label or technology changed.
